data.title: 3 out of 4 communications services stocks deliver EPS wins this week: Earnings Scorecard
data.description:
Communications services stocks grabbed the spotlight this week as Wall Street digested earnings reports from major names, including Alphabet (GOOG) and Verizon (VZ).

The communications services sector (XLC) lost over 14% so far this year, compared to the nearly 13% rise in the broader S&P 500 Index.

In this week's earnings recap, four tickers reported results, all of which three reported earnings beats. On the revenue side, two companies exceeded revenue expectations, while two companies trailed estimates.

Below are the latest quarterly reports from some key players, which reported results this week:

Alphabet (GOOG) (GOOGL) closed over 12% lower on Thursday following the tech giant’s release of the company's third-quarter financial results, which marked its first quarterly earnings miss since Q4 2022. Q3 earnings trailed Wall Street estimates, despite a more than doubling of Google Cloud revenue as demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure and services surged.

Verizon Communications (VZ) reported third-quarter revenue and adjusted earnings above analysts’ estimates, as well as stronger subscriber additions and higher margins that helped the telecom company lift its full-year 2026 guidance for a third consecutive quarter.

T-Mobile (TMUS) increased the number of new customers and saw higher average revenue per account (ARPA) leading to a 7.4% increase in third-quarter revenue and a 34% improvement in earnings, both of which beat Wall Street’s expectations.

For the upcoming week, Charter Communications (CHTR), Live Nation Entertainment (LYV), Fox (FOX), and News Corp (NWSA) are some communication services names that are scheduled to report quarterly results.

data.title: Morgan Stanley, Hyperliquid in gainers; Brazilian stocks, HSBC among decliners: week's financials warp
data.description:
Wall Street's major indexes declined at least 1% each this week amid a deep technology trade rout. State Street Financial Sel Sec SPDR ETF (XLF) advanced 1.09% during the week as earnings releases took center stage.

Among megacap financial stocks, Morgan Stanley (MS) topped the winners, advancing 2.68% week-over-week to close at $184.30. The stock climbed after winning a key role in the Anthropic IPO.

Mitsubishi UFJ Financial (MUFG) followed with a 2.33% rise to $21.56.

Mastercard (MA) was a significant gainer in the category, adding 2.31% from the previous week to $638.01. The stock has been gaining after the card payment network delivered Q3 top- and bottom-line beats as consumer spending continued to hold up.

HSBC (HSBC) led the decliners, retreating 5.80% to $85.42. The bank missed its Q3 non-GAAP EPS and revenue estimates.

Among largecap stocks, Brazilian stocks led the losers after President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva secured a fourth term in Sunday's presidential runoff, defeating right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro and overturning market expectations of a shift toward more conservative economic policies.

Banco Bradesco (BBD) (-37.35% W/W to $2.55), Itaú Unibanco (ITUB) (-26.27% W/W to $7.13), Nu (NU) (-23.42% W/W to $11.61), and Banco Santander (Brasil) (BSBR) (-20.54% W/W to $4.41) topped the decliners.

Evercore (EVR) (+15.33% W/W to $290.50), SoFi Technologies (SOFI) (+14.68% W/W to $16.76), and Blue Owl Capital (OWL) (+10.36% W/W to $10.33) were the top gainers in the category on the back of strong quarterly result announcements.

Hyperliquid Strategies (PURR) led the midcap gainers, advancing 25.40% to $11.01.

The week saw Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) enter an agreement to bring Trade[XYZ]'s perpetual markets onshore in the U.S. Trade[XYZ] is a deployer of real-world-asset perpetual markets on Hyperliquid.

Famed hedge fund manager Stanley Druckenmiller, in his first post on X, touted the pending launch of 24/7 perpetual futures on Hyperliquid in the U.S. as an innovative product.

Porch Group (PRCH) added 15.96% to close the week at $20.56 on the back of a Q3 earnings beat.

Brazilian financial products and services provider XP (XP) (-53.01% W/W to $14.29) led the midcap decliners.

For the smallcap stocks, Inter (INTR) (-44.23% W/W to $4.01), Agi (AGBK) (-32.06% W/W to $5.15), TOP Financial (TOP) (-27.34% W/W to $11.11), Vinci Compass Investments (VINP) (-23.41% W/W to $8.80), Better Home & Finance (BETR) (+24.64% W/W to $20.84), MidCap Financial (MFIC) (+23.63% W/W to $10.36), and Stewards (SWRD) (+19.20% W/W to $2.98) were the notable movers.

data.title: Meta is said to form bipartisan influence group ahead of elections
data.description:
Meta (META) is building a bipartisan group of former political operatives ahead of midterm elections as the Facebook owner seeks to deepen its relationships with both Democrats and  Republicans, Axios reported on Saturday.

According to sources, Meta (META) president and vice chairman Dina Powell McCormick, a former bank executive who served the first Trump administration, is spearheading a new recruitment drive to achieve the goal. 

The hiring initiative under Powell McCormick saw Michael Hacker, a longtime aide to House Democratic power broker Jim Clyburn, joining Meta (META) as VP of compute initiatives. Also, Nick Schmit, a former top aide to the Biden Administration’s Commerce Secretary Gina Raimondo, joined as director of strategic partnership management.

The company has also added several former Trump administration officials, including Pat Trueman, a senior official on Trump's 2024 presidential campaign who joined Meta's U.S. policy operation. Meanwhile, Josh Raffel, who worked with Powell McCormick during the first Trump administration, was also recently hired as VP of compute initiatives.

There was a slew of promotions aimed at facilitating the transition. While Powell McCormick recently added external affairs to her portfolio, the company promoted Brian Rice, a former aide to Democratic Secretary of State John Kerry, to lead its U.S. government affairs.

Tucker Bounds, who served on John McCain's presidential campaign, was elevated to the position of head of global communications, while C.J. Mahoney, a former Trump administration official, was named Meta's (META) chief legal officer in January.

Mahoney, who served as deputy U.S. Trade Representative during the first Trump administration, has assumed additional policy responsibilities since then.

According to sources, Meta (META) CEO Mark Zuckerberg and Powell McCormick met with the Democratic House Commission on Artificial Intelligence and the Innovation Economy in August following an invitation from Rep. Josh Gottheimer (D-N.J.).

The discussions with Gottheimer and other Democrats who co-chair the commission focused on the company's AI strategy, including its infrastructure build-out and economic investment plans.

The meeting and the recruitments underscore Meta’s (META) efforts to influence U.S. politics amid growing public scrutiny over artificial intelligence and data center buildout ahead of the midterm elections.

Dear readers, we recognize that politics often intersects with the financial news of the day, so we invite you to click here to join the separate political discussion.

data.title: Communication services sector declines in October; Reddit leads losses
data.description:
The communication services (XLC) declined over 9% in October amid a turbulent sell off fueled by growing investor scrutiny over the massive AI-related investments and disappointing results from big names including Alphabet and Meta Platforms.

Communication Services Sector October Scorecard

  • Sector Return: -9.9%
  • Best Performer: EchoStar (+9.86%)
  • Worst Performer: Reddit (-38.70%)
  • Top Theme: Corporate results and AI-related sell-off

Seeking Alpha analyst Dividend Collection Agency, Contributing analyst to the iREIT+Hoya Capital investment group believes October's decline is the continuation of investor's for returns on AI spending amid elevated inflation and interest rates.

“With the potential to see the Fed raise rates again before year end, investor's will likely to continue focusing on cash flow and balance sheet preservation vs strong top and bottom line growth.”

Top communication services performers of the month

On the individual front, EchoStar (ECHO) was the biggest winner, followed by Walt Disney (DIS) and Omnicom (OMC). Last month, UBS upgraded EchoStar to Buy from Neutral and raised its price target to $150 from $127, citing the value of the company’s expected SpaceX (SPCX) stake and remaining spectrum holdings.

Here are the top five gainers of the month:

  • EchoStar (ECHO) +9.85%
  • Walt Disney (DIS) +9.48%
  • Omnicom (OMC) +8.78%
  • Comcast (CMCSA) +7.14%
  • Live Nation Entertainment (LYV) +6.62%

Top communication services losers of the month:

On the other hand, Reddit (RDDT) was the biggest detractor in the quarter, slipping over 38%. The social media platform reported third-quarter revenue and earnings above estimates, while daily active user growth slowed and its fourth-quarter revenue forecast fell short of analysts’ expectations.

AppLovin claimed the second spot, while Alphabet was third in the list.

The analyst said that Reddit's decline was likely due to management's comments, which didn't give investors much confidence going forward.

“This overshadowed the 53% growth in revenue year-over-year. The decline in Referral traffic and anticipation for this to decline double-digits in the upcoming quarter were not positive signs,” said analyst Dividend Collection Agency.

Here are the top five detractors of the quarter:

  • Reddit (RDDT) -38.70%
  • AppLovin (APP) -18.77%
  • Alphabet (GOOGL) -17.27%
  • Meta Platforms (META) -15.28%
  • Skydance (SKYD) -14.99%

data.title: Alphabet’s record plunge, Intel’s 30% collapse: tech’s brutal week of reckoning
data.description:
A broad selloff in technology stocks gathered pace this week, with chipmakers, cloud computing groups, cybersecurity companies and software providers all sharply lower. Several of the sector’s biggest names lost billions of dollars in market value after reporting earnings or issuing forecasts that disappointed investors

The iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF (IGV) fell 5.52% for the week, while the Dow Jones U.S. Software Index lost more than 3%. The Nasdaq Composite declined 1.95%, as of mid-day Friday.

Star analyst Dan Ives described the week as “absolutely brutal” for technology investors, saying the disruption from AI was becoming increasingly visible in corporate earnings.

Alphabet (GOOGL) suffered its biggest one-day percentage decline on record on Thursday, falling as much as 13% and wiping out roughly $500B in market value. Google reported a rare earnings miss on slower growth in search advertising and a sharp increase in AI spending.

Intel (INTC) shares plunged about 30% on Friday after the chipmaker issued a fourth-quarter forecast well below Wall Street expectations, warning that weakness in the personal computer market could persist through the first half of 2027. 

INTC decline also dragged down semiconductor stocks. The PHLX Semiconductor Sector index (SOX) fell 9%. AMD (AMD) dropped 11%, Broadcom (AVGO) and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM) each fell 6%, and Micron (MU) and Nvidia (NVDA) each lost 5%. SanDisk (SNDK) shares fell 12% on Friday despite reporting better-than-expected quarterly results and issuing stronger guidance and an eight-for-one stock split.

Amazon (AMZN) shares shed roughly 7% following its earnings report, as its aggressive investment plans overshadowed growth in its cloud computing business.  Microsoft (MSFT) offered a relative bright spot, with shares down about just 2% since its results. Though it moved to raise $25B through a bond offering.

ServiceNow (NOW) shares tumbled more than 25% on Thursday after the enterprise software company issued a weaker-than-expected forecast for subscription growth, reviving concerns about the potential impact of AI on traditional software businesses.

Fortinet (FTNT) shares plunged about 27%. Although the company beat third-quarter earnings and revenue estimates, investors were disappointed by slower product revenue growth and a reduction in its full-year services revenue outlook. 

Selloff spread to other software and cybersecurity companies, with Zscaler (ZS) falling 7.5%, Okta losing 7.1%, Rubrik declining 5.3%, Palo Alto Networks dropping 5%, Cloudflare shedding 4.9%, CrowdStrike falling 4.6% and SentinelOne losing 3.5%, since Thursday.  Twilio (TWLO) shares tumbled 19% on Friday despite the company beating third-quarter earnings and revenue estimates, but analysts called its smaller-than-expected beat.

The tech sell-off represented a moment for long thought rather than a full market reckoning, according to Matt Orton, chief market strategist at Raymond James.

"This pivotal tech earnings week has been a tale of two cities for tech investors…bringing a painful week to the tech bulls although the underlying drivers of the AI Revolution are even more defined going forward in our view," Ives said.

data.title: Okta to replace Kenvue in S&P 500
data.description:
The identity management and security company Okta (OKTA) is expected to debut in the S&P 500 (SP500) next week, replacing consumer healthcare firm Kenvue (KVUE), which is being delisted following its proposed $40B sale to Kimberly-Clark (KMB).

In a statement late Friday, the S&P Dow Jones Indices announced that the changes will take effect before the markets open on Nov. 4 alongside several other revisions to the S&P MidCap 400 (MDY) and S&P SmallCap 600 (VIO).

In the S&P SmallCap 600 (VIO), McGrath RentCorp (MGRC) will replace Glaukos (GKOS), as the glaucoma treatment developer is set to join the S&P MidCap 400 (MDY), replacing the latest S&P 500 entrant, Okta (OKTA).

Also in the S&P SmallCap 600 (VIO), Loar Holdings (LOAR) is set to replace LiveRamp Holdings (RAMP), which is being acquired by Publicis (PUBGY) (PGPEF) in a $2.5B deal scheduled to close soon.

Having more than doubled in value, San Francisco, California-based Okta (OKTA) is expected to extend its YTD rally ahead of its anticipated inclusion in the S&P 500 (SP500) as funds that track the benchmark index adjust their holdings to reflect the new entrant.

data.title: OpenAI slashes funding goal by $10B amid tech selloff: FT
data.description:
OpenAI (OPENAI) has cut the target for its newest funding round by $10B at a time when the U.S. tech stocks are in a selloff driven by concerns over AI infrastructure buildout, The Financial Times reported, citing people with knowledge of the matter.

The ChatGPT maker is now looking for about $20B in funds at a valuation of roughly $1.25T, down from $1.4T it targeted last month, according to the report. While the company set a Friday deadline for investors to commit, the “first close” is expected to generate ⁠less than $20B after some investors cut their allocations, it ​added.

OpenAI (OPENAI) didn’t immediately respond to a request for comments. Last week, citing people familiar with the deal, CNBC reported that the San Francisco-based AI firm is closing in on a funding round that could raise up to $30B.

The company that is seeking a U.S. listing next year was racing to close the funding round partly to get ahead of rival Anthropic’s (ANT) much-anticipated public debut in mid-November, Reuters had reported previously.

Its revised funding target reflects investor worries over the pace of AI buildout.  The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) fell 2% this week, its third straight weekly drop, as quarterly results from Intel (INTC) and Amazon (AMZN) showed the pace of their massive cash burn amid heavy investments in AI-related development.

data.title: Amazon and Google both have custom chips. Here's what they said about their future.
data.description:
Amid their respective surges in artificial intelligence-related spending, Amazon (AMZN) and Alphabet (GOOG) (GOOGL) have seen strong internal demand for their respective custom chip businesses. 

Both companies still rely heavily on Nvidia (NVDA) for access to GPUs and will likely continue to do so for the foreseeable future. However, it's clear the ambitions of both companies go beyond just internal use to generate revenue. Alphabet started selling its tensor processing units externally earlier this year, and Amazon is set to do so with its Trainium offerings in late 2027. 

And given the insatiable demand for GPUs and CPUs to run AI models, agents, and more, both tech titans see promising futures that could generate billions of dollars in added revenue.

'Strong demand' for TPUs, with more to come?

For Alphabet, its TPU systems have seen “strong demand” already, CEO Sundar Pichai said. The company started offering them externally starting in the middle of this year.

“We are working hard to bring more capacity online to meet this long-term demand,” Pichai said on the company's third-quarter earnings call. “At the same time, we are seeing strong demand for our TPU systems across a wide range of customers, and we expect that to continue as we scale.”

The company has worked with tech giants such as Meta (META) and Apple (AAPL), AI model labs like Mirendil and Physical Intelligence, and financial firms like Citadel Securities to utilize its TPUs. In total, nearly 100 customers already use TPUs, and the company expects that trend to continue.

“Given continued strong and accelerating demand, we've recently entered into partnerships to deliver TPU systems with both Crux AI and Oracle, with more in the works,” Google Cloud CEO Thomas Kurian said on the earnings call.

Yorkville Ives analyst Dan Ives said he was pleased regarding the demand for TPU systems that Alphabet is already seeing, citing it as a “second growth engine on the field the other hyperscalers do not have.”

In recent memory, Alphabet has expanded the distribution for TPUs, including deals with Oracle (ORCL) and Crux AI, Kurian explained. And while the company declined to provide specific financial information for TPU sales, CFO Anat Ashkenazi said there will be a “meaningful revenue ramp in 2027.”

Amazon's chips are growing at triple digits

Amazon said in July that its custom chips business (which includes Graviton and Trainium) had reached a $25B revenue run rate. This week, the company delved further into detail and said chip-related revenue grew at a triple-digit percentage pace year-over-year.

Revenue commitments from its Graviton CPUs and Trainium AI accelerators have each risen more than 20 times. By bringing Trainium outside of Amazon Web Services later next year, that could expand its market considerably, Amazon added.

Amazon CEO Andy Jassy explained “most customers are going to use multiple models,” and said its approach is different from Alphabet when it comes to selling chips externally versus what is used in the cloud. (There is still strong demand for older generations of Amazon's Trainium chips that support the economic longevity of the existing infrastructure.) 

“I would say that the number of companies who have a significant cloud business and a chip strong enough to sell externally is effectively two,” Jassy said on the company's earnings call, referring to Alphabet. “So there really aren't many customers that have to grapple with the same type of problem at this type of scale. And at this point, everybody is producing their advanced chips with the same provider. There's only so many chips that provider can provide each year. Everybody gets an allocation. And you have to decide with that allocation how much of it you want to sell externally and how much of it you want to use in your cloud. And there's a trade-off. If you sell externally, you're able to realize more revenue in the short term because you get to recognize the revenue as soon as it leaves your inventory. And on the flip side, if you decide to use it inside your cloud in the form of EC2 instances or Bedrock, you actually will end up driving more absolute revenue and free cash flow from those chips because you get to use them over 5 to 6 years and drive revenue for a longer period of time. You have to really think through what you want to do. To date, I would say that we've taken a different approach in how we've used our chips than the other provider who has the same type of balancing act going on.”

“Our ability to create price performance, scalable chips is going to be a very significant strategic advantage for us at scale, both in our own cost structure as well as building a separate business. And selling external chips really is a very different business than your cloud infrastructure business,” Jassy added.

data.title: ServiceNow CFO says AI disruption to enterprise software narrative is false
data.description:
ServiceNow (NOW) Chief Financial Officer and President Gina Mastantuono understands the importance of guardrails when an enterprise wants to deploy AI solutions.

"Every business and industry needs a harness for AI," she said in an interview with Seeking Alpha. "Enterprise is very different from consumer. One mistake becomes disastrous in minutes. Ninety percent of organizations worldwide have already had an agentic security incident in the past year. Having the security in place is simply not optional."

"We build safeguards into how we innovate," she added. "ServiceNow does that incredibly well. Our AI Control Tower gives customers the confidence and security to use AI without worry."

ServiceNow reported its third-quarter financial results and outlook on Wednesday night. Despite posting solid results, featuring another quarter of 20% plus year-over-year revenue growth, shares cratered 27% by the time the markets closed on Thursday, erasing three months of share gains in one session.

However, most financial firms remain positive on the stock and the trajectory of the company.

"Key positives are centered around the strong AI activity, with nnACV up 65% YoY, which prompted higher 2026 ACV guidance," said Bank of America analyst Tal Liani. "However, the focal points were the 120bp and 40bp shortfall in 4Q in cRPO and subscription growth guidance, partially explained by accounting and timing. We don't fully subscribe to management's explanation on the quarter's weakness, yet remain constructive on the stock, as we see clear evidence of AI growth and view these fluctuations as growing hiccups."

"With the company guiding to a deceleration in cRPO growth into F4Q and an incremental headwind into FY27, we believe the implied low-20% y/y revenue growth rate for F4Q and preliminary estimate for around 19% growth for FY27 (prior to embedding the acceleration in AI adoption into our estimates) still outlines a robust underlying business with room for upside led by performance, despite the concerns investors might express on a slowdown in the cRPO metric, which is largely on account of revenue drivers moving out of scope of cRPO to a modest extent on a temporary basis," said J.P. Morgan analyst Samik Chatterjee.

Despite the noise around the latest earnings and outlook, ServiceNow remains positive on its AI strategy. It remains model-agnostic, allowing customers to use the closed or open model of their choice. It also formed a new partnership with OpenAI (OPENAI). The partnership expansion includes a new ServiceNow plugin for ChatGPT, enabled by Action Fabric. The companies aim to develop security and risk solutions powered by OpenAI cyber models, a Codex integration in AI Workflow Factory, and voice-driven governance and risk assessment for ServiceNow's Super Intelligence Control Tower.

"Enterprises are deploying at scale, and our momentum continues to accelerate and be strong, but at the same time demand for our core workloads remains strong," Mastantuono said. "AI is pulling our core in a strong way. ServiceNow is able to develop and deploy AI without significant infrastructure investments that a lot of companies are having to spend."

data.title: Talking Costco: Why a special dividend might not be the right play
data.description:
Costco (COST) is widely anticipated to be close to teeing up a special dividend. The retailer started paying special dividends in December 2012 with a one-time payout of $7 per share, which cost about $3B. After that, the company paid $5 per share in February 2015 and $7 per share in May 2017. In November 2020, the board declared a $10 per share special dividend, and the largest one so far was the $6.7B payout in January 2024.

While some analysts and income-loving shareholders are expecting the next special dividend in 2027, Mizuho analyst David Bellinger asked whether the capital could be deployed more strategically elsewhere. 

Bellinger and his team think Costco (COST) is definitively behind others when it comes to e-commerce operations, rapid fulfillment, and retail media. "We believe management could address certain weaknesses and decelerating membership growth by re-routing what would likely be $8B to 9B from a special dividend back into the business," highlighted Bellinger. 

Specifically, Bellinger thinks Costco (COST) could use the funds to ramp up digital investments centered around rapid delivery options for groceries, as well as building out several hundred standalone gas stations to fuel member growth and solidify retention rates. Currently, Costco (COST) has one standalone gas station open in Mission Viejo, California, and has plans to build one in Honolulu.

In addition, the Mizuho analysts believe acquiring a high-margin advertising arm similar to what Walmart (WMT) has done with VIZIO and Vibe.co could stoke future growth and margins, as well as create pushback against the bearish narrative of under-investment by the Issaquah, Washington-based company.
